- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is flat or rising, lower forecast early to avoid lagging downside.  
- After a sharp price spike, reduce forecast momentum for next 3–5 days to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 3–5 days of high prices), adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day.  
- When sentiment is high but price drops sharply, assume model overestimates momentum — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >2% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction.  
- If sentiment is rising but price falls, model may be overconfident — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment aligns.
